findings.current_text: Idempotent acceptance and payment recording, so a retry never creates a second order or charge.
findings.problem: Idempotency covers acceptance and payment recording only. Settlement releases, refunds and the holdback release are calls to the payment company's API that POOL itself starts, and they have no duplicate or timeout rule. Nothing requires payment status to come from a verified payment-company callback rather than the browser's return page. The lifecycle marks orders 'CANCELLED (booking refunded)' (line 398) without waiting for confirmation that the refund went through. The risks are a double release, a double refund, and orders shown as paid or refunded when they are not.
findings.evidence: Master §30.2 line 1335: "Provider callbacks ... require signature validation, timestamp/replay controls, and unique provider event IDs. A timeout after a payment/payout request means the external result may be unknown ... never blindly send the money again." Master §34.4 line 1504: "Duplicate/unknown payment result | Hold further action | ... resolve uncertainty before retry". Master §28.4 lines 1217-1218: CANCELLED and refund receipt are separate facts, and REFUNDED means "full amount has been verified received". The blueprint's grep for 'webhook', 'signature', 'timeout' and 'retry' finds only line 971.
findings.proposed_change: Replace line 971 with: "- Idempotent acceptance and payment recording, so a retry never creates a second order or charge. Payment status comes only from the payment company's signature-checked webhook or a server-side status call, never from the browser's return page. Every release and refund carries one unique key per order and action. After a timeout, POOL checks the status before any retry. An order shows 'refunded' only once the payment company confirms it."
